transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, thank you. I made the appointment because... I've just started to feel, in a quiet but stubborn sort of way, that the best version of my life is behind me. I've always been a practical person, but lately it just seems like no amount of planning or discipline is going to get me back to feeling like myself again.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?

Yes, I'd say so. Most days, I'm not in tears or anything dramatic like that. It's more that... well, there's just this low, gray tone running underneath everything. I notice it even when I'm out in the studio, or just sitting across from my wife at dinner. It's just sort of always there.
Have you been getting less enjoyment from things you used to enjoy?

No, I wouldn't really say that. I still like doing the things I've always liked. I still enjoy my time out in the studio, or, you know, reading a good book. It's not that the activities themselves have lost their appeal... it's just that underlying mood I mentioned. But no, I haven't really noticed a loss of enjoyment.
Did this low mood begin after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

Yes, actually, it did. It started after I had a hiking injury... that was a little over three years ago. Let's see, probably about three years and three months now, to be exact. That's really when this whole feeling began.
Do you find yourself feeling upset mainly when you think about the hiking injury and how it changed your life?

No, not really. I mean, I don't spend much time dwelling on the injury itself these days. It was frustrating at the time, sure, but... I don't feel upset because I'm thinking about the accident or how it changed things. It's more that the low mood started around then and just sort of stuck around, regardless of what's actually on my mind.
Has this low, gray mood been present continuously for at least two years?
Yes, it has. Like I mentioned, it started a little over three years ago, and... well, it hasn't really lifted since then. It's just been pretty much a constant, steady thing day in and day out.
During the past three years, have you ever gone through a period of at least two weeks when your depression became much worse than your usual baseline?

No, I don't think so. It hasn't really spiked or gotten severely worse at any point. It's just been the same mild, gray feeling the whole time. Nothing that really stands out as a sudden drop for a couple of weeks.
